source_text:
καθ' ἡμέραν ἑνὸς ὑποκλεπτομένου. Κριοὶ δὲ δὴ πάλιν δύο καὶ ἀμνοὶ δεκατέσσαρες, χιμάρου τοῖς θύμασιν ἐπενηνεγμένου.
{ΚΥΡ.} Δυσκάτοπτος μὲν, ὦ Παλλάδιε, τῶν τεθεσπισμένων ὁ νοῦς, καὶ ἀμυδρὸν τῇ φύσει τὸ χρῆμά ἐστι. Πειράσομαι δὲ ὡς ἔνι, τό γε εἰς νοῦν ἧκον εἰπεῖν. Μεθαρμόσεις δὲ ὅ τι πρὸς τὸ ἄμεινον αὐτὸς, εἰ μὴ κατ' εὐθὺ διᾴττοιμι τοῦ σκοποῦ.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Διακείσομαι.
{ΚΥΡ.} Ἔοικε τοίνυν τὸ θεῖον ἡμῖν χρησμῴδημα τήν τε τῶν ἐξ Ἰσραὴλ ἐν νόμῳ παιδαγωγίαν, καὶ τῶν διὰ πίστεως εἰσκεκομισμένων εἰς ἁγιασμὸν ἀνατυποῦν τὴν κλῆσιν. Δηλοῖ δὲ, οἶμαί που, τῆς θυσίας τὸ αἴνιγμα, ὅτι δύο μὲν ἤστην καιροὶ καθ' οὓς ἂν νοοῖντο πεπαιδαγωγῆσθαι πρὸς θεογνωσίαν καὶ εἰς νομικὴν πολιτείαν, αἱ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἀγέλαι. Τίνες δ' ἂν εἶεν οἱ τοιοίδε καιροὶ, ἢ ἐκεῖνοί που πάντως καθ' ὃν ἦν ἔτι που Μωσῆς, Ἰησοῦς τε καὶ κριταὶ, καὶ καθ' ὃν οἱ προφῆται μέχρις Ἰωάννου τοῦ Βαπτιστοῦ, τοῦ καὶ περισσότερον ἔχοντος κατὰ τὴν τοῦ Σωτῆρος φωνὴν, ἀποστολῆς δηλονότι καὶ λειτουργίας προφητικῆς. Ἀλλ' ἐν καιροῖς τοῖς δυσὶν ὑπεμφαίνει τὸ Γράμμα τὸ ἱερὸν γεγενῆσθαί τινας βίου μὲν τρίβον ἰόντας τὴν ἐπαινουμένην ἐν νόμῳ, πλὴν οὐκ ἐν ἴσῳ μέτρῳ, καὶ εἰσάπαν ἐμφερεστάτην, δυνάμει τε καὶ εὐεξίᾳ πνευματικῇ. Οἱ μὲν γὰρ ἦσαν τῆς ἀνωτάτω τυχὸν, ἧς ἂν τύπος ὁ μόσχος. Ἕτεροι δὲ αὖ, τῆς ὡς ἐν μεσότητι νοουμένης. Σημεῖον δ' ἂν γένοιτό που καὶ τοῦδε, κριός. Καὶ τρίτοι πρὸς τούτοις, τῆς ἐπὶ βραχὺ μειονεκτουμένης καὶ ἐνυφιζάνοντι μέτρῳ, καθάπερ ἀμέλει παρέσται νοεῖν ὡς ἐν μεγέθει σωματικῷ τοῖς ἀμνοῖς. Ἢ γὰρ, οὐχὶ μείων μὲν μόσχου κριὸς, ὑποκάθηται δὲ τοῦ κριοῦ μέγεθος, ὁ ἀμνός;
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Φημὶ, πῶς γὰρ οὔ;
{ΚΥΡ.} Οὐκοῦν τῆς ἑκάστου ποσότητος, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι τῆς ἐν ἐπιεικείᾳ, τύπος ἂν εἴη καὶ μάλα σαφὴς, τὰ ὠνομασμένα τῶν ζώων. Ἐπειδὴ δὲ τὸ προὖχον ἀεὶ καὶ ἀπόλεκτον, μεῖόν πως ἐν ἀριθμῷ, τοῦ δευτέρου δὲ καὶ τρίτου, σπάνιον γὰρ, ταύτῃτοι τρισκαίδεκα μόσχοι, δέκα δὲ οἱ κριοὶ, καὶ δεκατέσσαρες οἱ ἀμνοί. Ἐπειδὴ δὲ δύο τοὺς κριοὺς εἶναί φαμεν, ἐν διπλῷ τῶν θυμάτων ὁ ἀριθμός. Ἀντὶ γὰρ ἀμνῶν ἑπτὰ, δεκατέσσαρες οἱ μόσχοι, δύο γε μὴν, οἱ κριοί· ἢ οὐκ εἰκὸς σεπτούς τε καὶ ἱεροὺς γενέσθαι πολλοὺς, καὶ κατά γε τὴν ἐν νόμῳ δικαιοσύνην αὐχοῦντας τὸ ἄμεμπτον; καθάπερ ἀμέλει περί τε Ζαχαρίου καὶ τῆς Ἐλιζάβετ ὁ θεῖος ἡμῖν γέγραφεν εὐαγγελιστὴς, ὅτι «Ἦσαν δίκαιοι ἀμφότεροι ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ, πορευόμενοι ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ἐντολαῖς καὶ δικαιώμασι τοῦ Κυρίου, ἄμεμπτοι.»
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Φημί· καὶ γάρ που Θεὸς τὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων μητέρα κατῃτιᾶτο λέγων· «Πῶς ἐγένου πόρνη, πόλις πιστὴ Σιὼν, πλήρης κρίσεως, ἐν ᾗ δικαιοσύνη ἐκοιμήθη ἐν αὐτῇ;»
{ΚΥΡ.} Ἦν οὖν ἄρα δικαιοσύνη κατὰ νόμον, καθ' ἢν καὶ εἰκὸς γενέσθαι δοκιμωτάτους ἐν ὑπακοῇ Θεοῦ,
pass_a_gloss: (in decrease) one being stolen away each day. And rams again two, and lambs fourteen, a he-goat being added to the victims. CYR.: Hard to discern, Palladius, is the sense of the things decreed, and dim by nature is the matter. But I will try, as is possible, to say what has come to mind. And you yourself will adjust whatever toward the better, if I should not dart straight at the target. PALL.: I will be so disposed. CYR.: The divine oracle then seems to portray for us both the training in law of those from Israel and the calling of those brought in through faith into sanctification. And the riddle of the sacrifice shows, I think, that two were the times in which the flocks of the Jews would be understood to have been trained toward knowledge of God and into the legal citizenship. And which would such times be, or surely those in which Moses was still, and Joshua and judges, and in which the prophets until John the Baptist, the one having even more according to the voice of the Savior, (more than) apostleship namely and prophetic ministry. But in the two times the sacred letter hints that some came to be going the path of life praised in law, but not in equal measure, and altogether most alike, in power and spiritual good condition. For some were of the highest perhaps, of which the calf would be a type. And others again of the one understood as in the middle. And of this too a sign would be the ram. And thirds besides these, of the one falling short a little and of a sinking measure, as indeed it will be possible to understand as in bodily size in the lambs. For is not the ram less than a calf, and the lamb sits below the size of the ram? PALL.: I say so, for how not? CYR.: So of the quantity of each, plainly of the one in goodness, a type and very clear would be the animals named. And since the excellent and choice is always somehow less in number than the second and third, for it is rare, therefore thirteen calves, and ten (read: two) the rams, and fourteen the lambs. And since we say the rams to be two, in double is the number of the victims. For instead of seven lambs, fourteen are the calves (read: lambs), and two indeed the rams; or is it not likely that many became august and holy, and boasting of the blamelessness according to the righteousness in law? Just as indeed concerning Zechariah and Elizabeth the divine evangelist has written to us that 'They were both righteous before God, going in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord, blameless.' PALL.: I say so; for also somewhere God accused the mother of the Jews saying: 'How did you become a harlot, faithful city Zion, full of judgment, in which righteousness slept in her?' CYR.: There was then a righteousness according to law, according to which it is also likely that some became most approved in obedience to God (continues).
pass_b_english: Palladius: …by one taken away each day, while the rams, again, are two and the lambs fourteen, with a goat added to the victims?

Cyril: The sense of what was decreed is hard to make out, Palladius, and the matter is obscure by nature. But I will try, as far as I can, to say what has come to my mind. You yourself will adjust it for the better if I do not shoot straight at the mark.

Cyril: Well, then, the divine oracle seems to portray for us both the training under the law of those from Israel and the calling of those brought in through faith to sanctification. The riddle of the sacrifice shows, I think, that there were two periods in which the flocks of the Jews may be understood to have been trained toward the knowledge of God and into the way of life under the law. And what would these periods be, if not surely the one in which Moses was still alive, and Joshua and the judges, and the one in which the prophets came, down to John the Baptist, who had something more, as the Savior said (Matthew 11:9), than an apostle’s mission and a prophet’s ministry? But the sacred Scripture hints that in the two periods there were some who walked the path of life praised in the law, yet not in equal measure, nor at all closely alike in strength and spiritual vigor. Some, perhaps, were of the highest measure, of which the calf would be a type; others again of the measure understood as middle, and of this too the ram would be a sign; and a third group besides, of the measure that falls a little short and sits lower, as one can see, of course, in the lambs, as to bodily size. For is not a ram smaller than a calf, and does not the lamb fall below the ram in size?

Cyril: So the animals named would be a very clear type of the measure of each person, clearly of his measure in goodness. And since what always stands out and is choice is somehow fewer in number than the second and the third, for it is rare, that is why there are thirteen calves, [two] rams, and fourteen lambs. And since we say that the rams are two, the number of the victims is doubled: instead of seven lambs, there are fourteen [lambs], and the rams are two. Or is it not likely that many became august and holy, and could boast of being blameless according to the righteousness in the law? Just as, of course, the divine evangelist has written for us about Zechariah and Elizabeth: ‘They were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless’ (Luke 1:6).

Palladius: Yes; and God somewhere reproached the mother of the Jews, saying, ‘How has the faithful city Zion become a harlot, she who was full of judgment, in whom righteousness lodged?’ (Isaiah 1:21).
Cyril: There was, then, a righteousness according to the law, by which it is likely that some became most approved in obedience to God…
